results.note: Naxos CD with Hila Plitmann: four movements total 25:48. 2014 per Wikipedia list. Formation other (voice) is the derived one.
Flute, cello, piano, 2009, for the Dolce Suono Ensemble (Wikipedia); Innova CD 'Freedom' (Mimi Stillman), 3 movements 17:07.

Koch Int'l Classics 1992 CD (Apple 1009510720): last three tracks Annunciation, Atonement, Apotheosis total 27:36, matching the 28'00" and 3 movements of the G. Schirmer work list; commissioned by CMS Lincoln Center, premiered Jan 1989 (Emerson Quartet, Ken Noda). Streaming credits on the disc are muddled but the album title names the Piano Quintet.

Delos DE3528 (Shifrin, Dover Quartet) 18:47. The Delos booklet and MusicWeb title it 'Clarinet Quintet' with the subtitle 'The Last Jew in Hamadan'; booklet dates it 2015, UNC quintet database 2016 (premiere 14 July 2016, Chamber Music Northwest).
IMSLP: flute, violin, 2 violas, cello; André, Offenbach [1818], plate 3840. CPO recording: No. 3 = 15:23, shortest of the three (No. 1 21:17, No. 2 19:40).
Op. 40 confirmed (Wikipedia list; three recordings). Recordings run 21:16-24:51; 22 is fine.
Op. 40 No. 2 is the only minor-key quartet; recordings 20:00-24:21.
Recorded on four discs, incl. single-work couplings (ASV Daniel Smith 19:48; Martusciello, Bongiovanni 'Works for Bassoon & Strings' 19:05); CRD 18:42; Bongiovanni Anjos 16:35.
CPO (Anna Kaiser) 23:04; RBM 'Danzi: Chamber Music' lists it as Op. 71, P. 263. Op. 71 = Three Trios for flute and strings (Wikipedia).
CPO 19:12; finale All'ungarese as stated.
CPO 13:34, four short movements, shortest of the set.
RBM CD track list: 'Trio for Violin, Horn & Bassoon in F Major, Op. 23, P. 304', six movements, total 26:11. Op. 24 only as the Simrock reprint per Boosey/Trevco (as the entry says).
Kronos (Nonesuch) track is one piece of 10:46; the composer's site lists it as 'for string quartet and tape (1992)'. A single piece of about 12 minutes or less is form short, not work.

Composer's site: 'solo oboe and chamber ensemble (1991)'; Wikipedia list: oboe, flute (piccolo), bass clarinet, violin, cello, percussion, piano. Recorded on Equilibrium CD 'American Byways' (2012; listed on the composer's recordings page), 14:00; the Audiophile Audition review calls it an oboe concerto with chamber ensemble.

Violin, viola, percussion (2006), three movements (Magic, Fifty-Five Minutes Past Midnight, Wig Dance) 9:49 on Equilibrium 'American Byways'; Audiophile Audition review confirms the trio scoring. The disc's artist credit is the UCO Wind Symphony but the review shows these are the chamber versions.

Violin, cello, piano (2006); Equilibrium 'American Byways' has it as a single 11:40 track (the same disc splits Diamond in the Rough by movement), so it is a single piece of about 12 minutes: form short. Reviewer calls it reminiscent of late 19th-century salon music.
Composer's site: 'string quartet and pre-recorded sound (1993)'; Wikipedia list notes the version with three Elvis impersonators and baritone sax. Kronos, Nonesuch 'Released 1985-1995', 8:24.

IMSLP: horn, 2 violins, viola, cello; Bochsa pere, Paris, n.d. (ca. 1813-19). Two recordings: Denabian/Quartetto Delfico (Musurgia, 30:02) and Peter Arnold (Rudolf Bayer, 28:48). Year left blank (no composition date found).

IMSLP and the Australian Music Centre date McLibel 2000 (alto saxophone, violin, viola, double bass, playback). Topology, 'Perpetual Motion Machine' (2003; MusicBrainz lists a 7:57 take). Entry year was blank.
Doric Quartet, Chandos CHAN 10873: 19:33; 2003 per Wikipedia (revised 2004).
String quartet and soprano (2013) per Wikipedia; Chandos CHAN 10873 (Doric, Allison Bell) 19:46. Formation note matches the Schoenberg precedent.

Boosey: Epitaphs (2010) for 2 violins, 2 violas, cello, premiered 12 July 2010 with Brett Dean viola and the Australian String Quartet; Chandos lists 'premiere recording' with Dean as solo viola II (22:10).
2019 per Wikipedia; Affinity Quartet, Da Vinci Classics, five movements 22:38.
Voxare Quartet, Albany TROY1685-86 'March to Tonality' (2017): three movements 28:31. Year left blank (not found).
Peskanov, Nicolas, Beck; four movements Aria-Vivace, Aria-Lento, Fuga, Reminiscence total 35:52.

IMSLP (Lamfalussy edition of the Liege manuscript): violin 1 or flute, violin 2, continuo. Ensemble Solstice, Arts/Scene 2011, Sonate a tre II = 10:48.

Track title 'DSCH (1969) for Clarinet, Trombone, Violoncello and Piano', 5:59, Moscow Conservatory Records 2021. Only this one recording found.
Sonnambula/Weinfield, AVIE AV2746 (Sept 2025; a commercial label, not self-released): Fantasia No. 4 (a 5), VdGS No. 1, 5:14; AVIE credits Dering. IMSLP: five viols (2 trebles, 2 tenors, bass).

Oboe, clarinet, two violins, viola, cello and tape, 2007 (ru.wikipedia); Quartz Music 'The Leaden Echo' 10:05.

Year and numbering conflict. Entry year 1782-83 comes from a MusicWeb review of the Ricercar disc; IMSLP, BnF and RISM show prints by Gaveaux (1797, 'Trois trios ... 1ere suite') and Imbault ([1800], six trios), with no earlier print found. 'Op. 66' appears on the Ricercar track list and the Billaudot edition (BnF uniform title '3 trios ... Op. 66'), but Op. 66 is also Devienne's flute quartets (IMSLP, Accent recording; catalogue ids 102803-102806), and in the Billaudot first suite No. 1 is G major, not D major. Recording fine: Le Petit Trianon, Ricercar RIC416 (2020). Recorded 15:05; minutes ok. Aka 'Op. 66 No. 1' for D major is the weakest (IMSLP numbers it No. 4).

IMSLP and Wikipedia: commissioned by the La Scala String Quartet for Verdi's bicentenary, premiered at La Scala 27 May 2013 (Sole 24 Ore review cited); three movements, 12-13 min.
